benchmarks/bench_batching.py.docstring:
Embedding throughput under three batching strategies, on real function chunks.

    uv run --extra dense python benchmarks/bench_batching.py

A padded batch costs (items x longest item), and code units are heavily skewed in length
(django: p50 63 tokens, p99 650). The strategies differ only in how items are grouped:

- arrival: fixed-size batches in file order, what a per-file indexing loop would do
- sorted:  one global length sort, fixed batch size (sentence-transformers' default)
- budget:  global length sort, batches packed up to a token budget (allfather)

benchmarks/bench_reranker_cpu.py.docstring:
Can the fine-tuned reranker run without a GPU? CPU latency and ranking fidelity, fp32 vs int8.

    uv run --extra dense python benchmarks/bench_reranker_cpu.py [--adapter models/ce_adapter] [--n 30]

Dynamic int8 quantization (torch.ao) stores every Linear layer's weights in 8 bits and
quantizes activations on the fly: a quarter of the memory and usually faster matrix products
on CPU. This scores validation issues (never used for training) three ways: on the GPU in
bf16 (the reference the evaluation uses), and on the CPU in fp32 and int8. It reports seconds
per query and how often each CPU variant agrees with the reference and finds the fix first.

benchmarks/bench_search.py.docstring:
Where does query time go, and would approximate search (HNSW) help?

    uv run --extra dense --with faiss-cpu python benchmarks/bench_search.py

Pruning algorithms (WAND/MaxScore for BM25, HNSW's best-first graph search for vectors)
trade index-build work and a little recall for faster scoring. That pays off when one index
serves many queries over a large corpus. Here every SWE-bench issue has its own commit, so
an index serves one query, and a snapshot holds tens of thousands of units. This measures
both sides on a real django snapshot whose unit embeddings are already cached.

scripts/browser_ltr.py.docstring:
Train the website's rankers: learning to rank on signals a browser can compute.

    uv run --extra dense python scripts/browser_ltr.py

Training data: SWE-bench minus Lite (12 projects) and the SWE-rebench "train" sample (119
other projects). Held out and run once at the end: SWE-bench Lite, and SWE-rebench "test",
30 projects no model ever saw. Cross-validation folds are split by project, so every choice
is judged on projects the model did not train on, which is what the website faces.

The website runs these stages (web/src/engine/rank.ts computes identical features):
  instant   keyword and mention signals; answers in milliseconds, before anything else is ready
  semantic  + static-embedding similarity over every function, computed in the background
  rerank    + MiniLM similarity for the top candidates; shipped only if it earns its download
  file      a ranker over files, for the Files view

scripts/ce_multilang.py.docstring:
Step 2 of ADR 0034: train and cross-validate reranker candidates on all six languages.

    uv run python scripts/ce_multilang.py records
    uv run python scripts/ce_multilang.py train --candidate B --fold 0     # on PACE, one job per fold
    uv run python scripts/ce_multilang.py score --candidate B --fold 0
    uv run python scripts/ce_multilang.py merge --candidate B
    uv run python scripts/website_rerank.py evaluate --multilang --name cand-B
    uv run python scripts/website_rerank.py evaluate --name cand-B         # the Python tasks

records: training examples from the reranker tasks of ADR 0021 (Python) and ADR 0034 (the five
other languages): each bug's query, the source of every function its fix changed, and its hard
negatives, the website pipeline's out-of-fold top 50 minus the fix. folds: five folds that keep
each project whole. train: one candidate (A, B or C, as ADR 0034 defines them) on four folds.
score: that candidate's adapter on the held-out fold's tasks, appended to the scores file the
evaluation reads. `--fold all` trains the final adapter on every project.

scripts/e1_grouped_cv.py.docstring:
E1 of ADR 0033: how optimistic is cross-validation grouped by issue rather than by project?

    uv run python scripts/e1_grouped_cv.py

Reads the ranker features saved by `allfather ltr` (SWE-bench test minus Lite, 1,941 issues, 12
projects) and cross-validates the same LambdaMART ranker three ways on the same matrix: five folds
of random issues (ADR 0006), five folds that keep each project together, and one fold per project.
No test set is read. Writes results/research/e1_grouped_cv.json.

scripts/e3_hint_strata.py.docstring:
E3 of ADR 0033: how much of each system's SWE-bench Lite score comes from reports that name the fix?

    uv run python scripts/e3_hint_strata.py

Descriptive only. Re-scores rankings already stored in results/ against Allfather's function-level
answer key, split by what the report says about the fix:

- function: it names a function the fix changes (its bare name, as a whole word)
- file: it names a file the fix changes (its path or file name), but no fixed function
- trace: it has a traceback, but names neither
- none: it names nothing the fix touches

No system is run and nothing is decided from this. Writes results/research/e3_hint_strata.json.

scripts/eval_import.py.docstring:
Bring an `allfather eval` result file into the shape scripts/frontier.py scores (ADR 0033, T0).

    uv run allfather eval --dataset fresh --gold data/fresh/gold_eval_python.jsonl         --retriever ltr-ce-more-data-notests --level function --out results/research/frontier/fresh_eval.json
    uv run python scripts/eval_import.py --set fresh --system allfather-fast --results results/research/frontier/fresh_eval.json

Keeps each issue's top 10; the result file has no per-issue latency.

scripts/export_showcase.py.docstring:
Pick the landing page's example searches from the evaluation run.

Real SWE-bench Lite issues where the full pipeline ranked a function the maintainers' fix changed
first, with a short title and an error or code line to show. Each entry keeps the pipeline's
actual top 4 from the run and which of them the fix changed. Deterministic: rerun after
export_site.py refreshes web/public/data/.

    uv run python scripts/export_showcase.py

scripts/export_site.py.docstring:
Export evaluation results and a code corpus as static JSON for the showcase site.

    uv run python scripts/export_site.py

Reads `results/*_lite_test.json` (written by `allfather eval`) and writes `web/public/data/*.json`.
The site is static: it replays these results, and its live search downloads and indexes
repositories in the visitor's browser, so it can be hosted anywhere without a server.

scripts/fresh_analysis.py.docstring:
The analysis of ADR 0033, for any set scripts/frontier.py and scripts/fresh_website.py have run.

    uv run python scripts/fresh_analysis.py --set pilot
    uv run python scripts/fresh_analysis.py --set fresh --threshold 0.62

RQ1: every system's function-level metrics with 95% intervals from a bootstrap over projects, and
paired tests against the reference (exact McNemar on yes/no metrics, a randomization test on MRR),
Holm-adjusted across the whole table. RQ2: mean cost and time per bug and the systems no other
beats on both accuracy and cost. RQ3: escalating the bugs the reference is least confident about to
each other system, across thresholds, against escalating the same number at random; --threshold
reports the operating point chosen beforehand on development data. RQ4: hit@10 by what the report
names. Writes results/research/analysis_<set>.json.

scripts/fresh_set.py.docstring:
Build fresh-2026, the sealed test set of ADR 0033.

    GITHUB_TOKEN=... uv run python scripts/fresh_set.py exclusions
    GITHUB_TOKEN=... uv run python scripts/fresh_set.py projects --per-language 17
    GITHUB_TOKEN=... uv run python scripts/fresh_set.py mine --created-after 2026-08-01 --until 2026-11-30
    GITHUB_TOKEN=... uv run python scripts/fresh_set.py full
    uv run python scripts/fresh_set.py seal --size 600 --agents 200

exclusions: every repository in any existing set, resolved to GitHub's repository ID (and its fork
parent), so a renamed or forked project is still excluded. Reads repository names only; the sealed
holdout's are taken from its manifest, never from its answer key.
projects: popular, active repositories per language that are not excluded.
mine: for each project, merged pull requests in the window that close exactly one issue opened
before them and after the cutoff, whose text was not edited after the pull request was opened; the
answer key is the merge diff's functions and files, tests excluded (ADR 0023's rule). Resumable.
seal: a random sample stratified by language, its agent subsample, and the manifest with hashes.
Nothing here runs a localizer.

scripts/fresh_website.py.docstring:
Run the website's own pipeline (ADR 0033, tier T0) on a set from scripts/frontier.py.

    uv run python scripts/fresh_website.py --set pilot
    uv run python scripts/fresh_website.py --set fresh --gpu results/website-rerank/gpu_config.json

The same ranking the live-accuracy monitor runs (browser rankers, semantic and language-model
stages), in all six languages. With --gpu, the top functions are also re-read by the GPU reranker's
adapters on this machine and blended into the order as the site does, for the languages and with
the depth and weight the configuration names (ADR 0034); the output is then <set>_website-gpu.jsonl.
With --files, each record also keeps the file ranker's top 10 (ADR 0033's file-level amendment), written
to <set>_website-files.jsonl. Writes results/research/frontier/<set>_website.jsonl otherwise. Resumable.

scripts/frontier.py.docstring:
Run frontier coding agents and models as bug localizers (ADR 0033, tiers T3 and T4).

    uv run python scripts/frontier.py pick --set pilot --n 10
    uv run python scripts/frontier.py run --set pilot --system claude-agent
    uv run python scripts/frontier.py score --set pilot

pick: a seeded sample of development issues (SWE-bench Verified minus Lite), never a test set.
run: for each issue, export the repository at its base commit with no git history, then ask the
system for the ten functions most likely to need the fix. Agents get read-only file tools and no
web access; single-call systems get no tools. Every run records the model, tokens, the
list-price cost the tool reports, wall time and the tools it used. Resumable.
score: hit@k, all@10 and MRR against the answer key, the unmapped-answer rate, and cost.

scripts/lca_bug_localization.py.docstring:
Allfather on Long Code Arena's bug-localization task (ADR 0035).

    uv run python scripts/lca_bug_localization.py rank --lang py --split train
    uv run python scripts/lca_bug_localization.py choose
    uv run python scripts/lca_bug_localization.py rank --lang py --split test
    uv run python scripts/lca_bug_localization.py score

`rank` runs the website's pipeline (browser configuration) on each bug and stores its file ranking,
the answer key, and the test file paired with each top file. On `train` it takes ADR 0035's random
150 bugs per language; on `test` it refuses to run before `choose` has fixed the setting. `choose`
picks k and the test rule on the training bugs by mean F1. `score` applies the chosen setting to the
test bugs, computes the leaderboard's metrics, and writes the answer files for the submission.

scripts/open_agent.py.docstring:
Open-weight models as bug localizers through a vLLM server (ADR 0033, open-model tier).

The agent gets the same three read-only abilities Claude Code gets in scripts/frontier.py: list
files by glob, search file contents, and read a range of lines. Every path is confined to the
bug's checkout. The single-call variant gets no tools. The server is any OpenAI-compatible
endpoint, normally `vllm serve` on the PACE node the job runs on, named by OPEN_MODEL_URL.

scripts/paper_tables.py.docstring:
Write every table and number the paper uses, from the committed results only.

    uv run python scripts/paper_tables.py

Reads results/research/analysis_<set>.json, the run records in results/research/frontier/ (for cost
and time), data/fresh/ (for the test set's composition) and the reranker study's choice.json, and
writes docs/paper/generated/: one .tex file per table and numbers.tex, a list of \newcommand macros
the text uses instead of typing numbers. Prices are the per-token rates listed in PRICES, with their
sources in the paper; a run on a subscription records no price, so its cost is computed from its own
token counts at those rates.

scripts/render_og.py.docstring:
Render web/public/og.png, the link-preview card, from the live page's hero section.

    npm --prefix web run build && npm --prefix web run preview &
    uv run --with playwright python scripts/render_og.py

Needs a Chromium for Playwright (`playwright install chromium`). Re-run after refreshing
web/public/data/, so the card shows current numbers.

scripts/rerank_choice.py.docstring:
Choose the six-language GPU reranker by ADR 0034's rule, from the saved fold scores.

    uv run python scripts/rerank_choice.py

For every scored configuration (the current Python-only pair and candidates A, B and C), the bugs are
ranked exactly as scripts/website_rerank.py evaluates them: depth and weight chosen on one half of the
projects, applied to the other, halves pooled. Per language it reports each configuration's function
hit@10, the paired exact test against the website pipeline with Holm's correction across languages,
and the paired test between configurations, so the choice compares them on the same bugs. Writes
results/website-rerank/choice.json.

scripts/rerank_long.py.docstring:
Apply ADR 0036's rule: does a reranker that reads more of the report beat candidate A?

    uv run python scripts/rerank_long.py

Every bug is ranked as the site ranks it: the website pipeline's out-of-fold top 50 blended with
the reranker's scores at the frozen depth and per-language weight of
results/website-rerank/gpu_config.json, nothing tuned. Candidate A (512 tokens of the report) is
compared with A-read2048 and L on the training bugs' out-of-fold scores, with the exact paired
test, on reports longer than 2,000 characters, on all bugs, and per language. Writes
results/website-rerank/long_reports.json.

scripts/restat.py.docstring:
Recompute the p-values the site publishes with the paired randomization test in metrics.py.

    uv run python scripts/restat.py

Reads only saved outcomes: the per-issue rows in results/browser_ltr_multilang/report.json and the
win/loss counts in results/website-rerank/*.json. No model runs and no test set is evaluated again.
Writes web/public/data/lite.json in place. The languages that use the learned ranker were chosen by
the cross-validation rule of ADR 0025 with the earlier test; that choice is recorded, not redone.

scripts/sample_rebench.py.docstring:
Pick the SWE-rebench bugs used to train and test the website's ranker.

    uv run python scripts/sample_rebench.py

150 random projects with at least 20 bugs each (none of SWE-bench's twelve, so SWE-bench
Lite stays untouched), up to 30 random bugs per project. Thirty projects are held out
entirely: "test" measures how the ranker does on projects it has never seen, which is what
the website faces. Seeded, and the result is committed, so the benchmark is reproducible.

scripts/swerank_export.py.docstring:
Export a set for SweRank's retrievers (ADR 0033, tier T1), in the per-issue BEIR layout they read.

    uv run python scripts/swerank_export.py --set fresh --out ../swerank-fresh

One folder per issue, named <prefix><issue id with unsafe characters replaced>, holding:
corpus.jsonl (every non-test function, method and class at the base commit, split by Allfather's
own chunker so both systems see the same units; _id is SweRank's "path/Class/method" form and the
text starts with the file path, as in the authors' corpora), queries.jsonl (the issue) and
qrels/test.tsv (the answer key). index.json maps folder names back to issue ids. Copy the output
directory to PACE and run cluster/swerank/retrieve.sbatch with DATA pointing at it.

scripts/swerank_full_queries.py.docstring:
Make SweRank's fresh-full data from its fresh data: the same corpora, the full bug reports as queries.

    uv run python scripts/swerank_full_queries.py --source $HOME/scratch/swerank/fresh --out $HOME/scratch/swerank/fresh-full

Every bug folder of the source keeps its corpus and answer key, linked rather than copied, and gets a
new queries.jsonl holding the bug's text from data/fresh-full (ADR 0033, full-report condition). It
refuses to run if a folder's current query is not the start of the full report, so the two conditions
can differ only in the report.

scripts/swerank_import.py.docstring:
Bring SweRank rankings for a set back into the shape scripts/frontier.py scores (ADR 0033, T1).

    uv run python scripts/swerank_import.py --set fresh --system swerank-embed-large --results results.json

The results file maps each issue id to SweRank document ids ("path/Class/method"), as written by
scripts/swerank_cached_retrieval.py with --prefix. Only the top 10 are kept. A run on a sealed set
is logged in results/test-evals.log.

scripts/time_relay.py.docstring:
Time whole-repository downloads through the site's relay.

    uv run python scripts/time_relay.py

Downloads each repository's .tar.gz at its current default-branch commit through
https://allfather.dev/relay three times and records the wall time and size of each. The first
download may miss Cloudflare's cache; later ones show the cached path. Network speed is the
laptop's own, so the file records it as measured, not as a property of the relay alone.

scripts/time_rerank.py.docstring:
Time the site's GPU reranker the way the browser calls it.

    uv run python scripts/time_rerank.py

Sends one request shaped like the browser's (a bug report and the text of 50 functions, here this
repository's own Python functions) to https://allfather.dev/rerank, then four more. Each request
carries a unique report, so none is answered from the one-day score cache. The first call shows
the start-up cost when no container is running; the rest are warm. Times include the network from
this laptop and the Worker hop.

src/allfather/rank/browser.py.docstring:
Ranking features a browser can compute, shared by the website and its training script.

The website (web/src/engine/rank.ts) computes exactly these for a repository it has indexed in
the visitor's browser; scripts/browser_ltr.py computes them here to train and evaluate the
model it runs. tests/test_site_engine.py checks the two agree feature by feature.

src/allfather/search/static.py.docstring:
Static embeddings (Model2Vec): a sentence vector is the weighted mean of token vectors.

No neural network runs at encode time, so a whole repository embeds in about a second, in
Python or in a browser. The website's ranker uses these for semantic search over every
function; web/src/engine/static.ts is the same computation, and the tests hold them equal.

tests/test_site_engine.py.docstring:
The website's JavaScript chunker must split code exactly like the Python package.

Runs the website's TypeScript engine (web/src/engine) under Node 24 on every Python file in
this repository plus a file of awkward constructs, and compares unit by unit.
